use_case_name: Resolve Dual Designations via Track Correlation

claims.content: To recognize and resolve air and surface track dual designations by having a C2 JU initiate track correlation, transmit a J7.2 Correlation message requesting other C2 IUs to perform correlation of the two tracks, and identify the TN to be retained and the TN to be dropped.

goal.raw_text: To recognize and resolve air and surface track dual designations by having a C2 JU initiate track correlation, transmit a J7.2 Correlation message requesting other C2 IUs to perform correlation of the two tracks, and identify the TN to be retained and the TN to be dropped.

claims.content: C2 JU
Two tracks are being reported to the interface and are eligible for correlation.
The dual designation is for air or surface tracks; the rules for land (ground) and space track dual designation resolution are TBD.
The C2 JU has the capability to perform common tracking in accordance with the correlation and decorrelation procedures and criteria.
The C2 JU has an automatic correlation capability for real-time air or surface tracks it originates.
When a C2 JU recognizes that two tracks which are being reported to the interface are eligible for correlation, it initiates action, either automatically or manually, to resolve the dual designation.

trigger.raw_text: When a C2 JU recognizes that two tracks which are being reported to the interface are eligible for correlation, it initiates action, either automatically or manually, to resolve the dual designation.

claims.content: All IUs periodically compare remote tracks to local tracks (and, optionally, to common local tracks) to determine if a dual designation has occurred.

All C2 JUs perform correlation and decorrelation of their local track data with respect to the remote data which they are receiving; the correlation process commences with comparing locally derived sensor data (position, velocity, and altitude) with the data received on the interface, in order to prevent or eliminate dual designations.

When a C2 JU recognizes that two tracks which are being reported to the interface are eligible for correlation, that JU initiates action, either automatically or manually, to resolve the dual designation.
The recognizing JU transmits the J7.2 Correlation message requesting all other C2 IUs to perform a correlation of the two tracks.

The J7.2 Correlation message identifies the TN to be retained and the TN to be dropped, and the originating JU indicates in the message if it has any constraint which would prohibit accepting a reverse correlation.

C2 JUs shall not automatically select as the TN to be dropped a TN which has any of the OCCs listed in paragraph 4.4.4.3.1g(6 7); in the absence of such a selection constraint, JUs shall select the higher TN as the TN to be dropped.

Receiving IUs accept the requested correlation unless certain prespecified conditions exist which require or allow the receiving IU to reject the requested correlation or respond with a reverse correlation request.

Two tracks shall pass the correlation tests and restrictions twice before the correlation is executed; when they pass once they are deemed a tentative correlation, are tested again upon the next correlation stimulus, and, if they pass the second correlation test with no correlation restriction, are processed for dual designation resolution in accordance with paragraphs 4.4.4.3.1j and k.

If prespecified conditions exist that require or allow rejection of the requested correlation, the receiving IU rejects the correlation and transmits the J7.2 message with the RV field set to value 2 to report the rejection.

If a receiving IU desires to reverse the requested correlation, it uses the RV field to determine if a reverse correlation request should be originated or if the original correlation request should be rejected; RV value 0 indicates a reverse correlation would be acceptable, and RV value 1 indicates a reverse correlation request would be rejected.
If the RV field is set to value 3, the correlation was manually initiated and shall be accepted unless certain conditions apply which require rejection.
If the Retained TN and the Dropped TN will decorrelate when subjected to the decorrelation criteria once, the correlation shall be rejected.

If there is an OCC on the Dropped TN and the received RV field is set to value 0, the reverse correlation shall be transmitted if the new Dropped TN has no correlation constraint; if both the Retained TN and Dropped TN have an OCC, the correlation shall be rejected.
If there is an OCC on the Dropped TN and the received RV field is set to value 1, the correlation shall be rejected.

If the above actions result in resolution of the ID conflict, the TN to be retained shall be tested for decorrelation in accordance with paragraph 4.4.4.3.2a before executing the correlation, except the test shall be conducted only once.

If the dual designation involves land (ground) or space tracks, the rules for land (ground) and space track dual designation resolution are TBD; exit the exception path with no resolution procedure specified for those tracks.

If prespecified conditions require or allow a receiving IU to reject the requested correlation, the receiving IU rejects the correlation and transmits the J7.2 message with the RV field set to value 2 to report the rejection; exit with the correlation request rejected.

If a receiving IU desires to reverse the requested correlation, it uses the RV field to determine whether to originate a reverse correlation request or reject the original correlation request: RV value 0 indicates a reverse correlation would be acceptable, and RV value 1 indicates a reverse correlation request would be rejected; exit by originating a reverse correlation request (RV=0) or by rejecting the original correlation request and transmitting the J7.2 message with the RV field set to value 2 to report the rejection (RV=1).

If the RV field is set to value 3, the correlation was manually initiated and shall be accepted unless certain conditions apply which require rejection; if such a condition applies, reject the correlation and transmit the J7.2 message with the RV field set to value 2 to report the rejection; exit with the correlation accepted or the rejection reported.
A J7.2 Correlation message has been transmitted by the recognizing C2 JU requesting all other C2 IUs to perform a correlation of the two tracks.
The J7.2 Correlation message identifies the TN to be retained and the TN to be dropped.
The receiving C2 IUs have accepted the requested correlation.
The two tracks have successfully passed the correlation tests and restrictions twice with no correlation restriction, and the correlation has been executed.

The TN to be dropped was not automatically selected from a TN having any of the OCCs listed in paragraph 4.4.4.3.1g(6 7); absent such a selection constraint, the higher TN was selected as the TN to be dropped.
For the track corresponding to the dropped TN, the C2 JU has ceased reporting the track and has transmitted a J7.0 (ACT = 0) Drop Track message on the surveillance TN.
